items.description: The split rule makes text inside double quotes never a command word, so `x="$(python3 -c 1)"`, which runs bare python, passes the hook. That violates the issue's Done-when at plan:19. The scanner must open a nested command context for `$(` and backticks inside double quotes.
items.plan_quote: Text inside single quotes, and text inside double quotes, is never a command word

items.description: The plan prescribes scanning heredoc bodies as ordinary lines with a regex or per-line split. That is not a shell lexer: apostrophes in heredoc bodies or comments desync quote state and hide later python3 calls, and the standard multi-line `git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF' ...)"` form is wrongly blocked. The correct outcome is one stateful awk scanner reading the command on stdin, with quote, comment, continuation, nested-context and heredoc states.
items.plan_quote: Lines of a heredoc body are scanned like ordinary lines (a heredoc fed to `bash` with a `python3` line would run it).

items.description: The plan says backslash escapes are honoured but never specifies backslash-newline continuation, so `uv run --no-project \<newline> python x.py` is read as one command with word `uv`. Continuation must be handled per lexer state inside the scanner (a comment ending in a backslash does not continue; a body line ending in a backslash does not stop a quoted heredoc), with one allowed and one blocked continuation test. Option-taking wrappers are a documented ceiling.
items.plan_quote: Backslash escapes outside single quotes are honoured when tracking quotes.
